chunks: That which the Sheikh — may Allah the Exalted support him — informed me of, saying: Ahmad b. Muhammad informed me, from his father, from Sa'd b. 'Abdullah, from Ahmad b. Muhammad, from al-Husayn b. Sa'id, from Safwan b. Yahya and Fadala b. Ayyub, from al-'Ala' b. Razin, from Muhammad b. Muslim, from one of them both (peace be upon them both):
He said: I asked him about a man who urinates but whose right hand has not touched anything — may he submerge it in water? He said: 'Yes, even if he is in a state of janaba.'
Meaning: when his hand is ritually pure — such is the indication of that (ruling).

key_terms.اَلْيُمْنَى: right [hand] — receives specific attention in purity law
key_terms.جُنُبًا: in a state of janaba — major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.طَاهِرَةً: ritually pure (tahira) — the operative condition for the ruling
key_terms.يَبُولُ: urinates — the act triggering the jurisprudential inquiry
key_terms.يَغْمِسُهَا: submerge it — immersion of a limb in a body of water

ai.seo_question: According to Shia hadith, can a man submerge his right hand in water after urinating if it has not touched anything impure, even while in a state of janaba?
ai.summary: Muhammad b. Muslim asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon them both) whether a man who urinated but whose right hand had not touched anything impure could submerge it in water. The Imam answered affirmatively, even if the man is in a state of janaba (major ritual impurity requiring ghusl). An appended clarification specifies that this permissibility is predicated on the hand being in a state of tahara (ritual purity).
